properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 8:46PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Sanford
to remain just below Minor flood stage. The river is forecast to
slowly climb into Minor flood stage later this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.5 feet, Water surrounds homes and covers some
driveways in the Stone Island area near Enterprise in Volusia
County. Water enters yards and floods docks in the River Oaks
Estates subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 5.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to Minor Flood Stage
early Friday morning, where it will linger near 5.5 feet into
early next week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at 1215 PM EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 8:45PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Geneva
Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate flood stage. A slow rise within
Moderate flood stage is forecast to continue through the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...Above Lake Harney...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 9.3 feet, Many secondary roads are flooded near Lake
Harney. Flooding in the Hatbill Road area near Loughman Lake.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 9.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Wednesday was 9.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 9.1 to 9.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 11 at 7:43PM CST until November 15 at 12:00PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Los Olmos Creek Near Falfurrias affecting Brooks County.

.Latest observations show that Low Olmos Creek near Falfurrias has
risen to Action Stage (5.0 feet) with a current level of 8.70 feet.
Levels are expected to remain above Action Stage likely through
Sunday morning, though forecast to begin decreasing Thursday morning.

For the Los Olmos Creek...including Falfurrias...elevated river
levels are forecast.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding reaches 120 feet wide
into flood plain-persons vulnerable to lowland flooding should move
equipment to higher ground At 9.0 feet, Flow is high enough to
close FM 1418 as water is covering the bridge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM CST Wednesday the stage was 8.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.8 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Action stage is 5.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at 100 PM CST.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 8:41PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused Major flooding at the gauge west of Cocoa. The river is
forecast to continue to rise within Major flood stage through this
weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 17.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 PM EST Wednesday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue rising, cresting at
17.2 feet this weekend.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 8:34PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall that has occurred upstream has resulted in continued
river levels in Minor Flood Stage. River levels are expected to
remain steady into the weekend as a large volume of water works north
through the basin, though developing northerly winds could generate a
small rise.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Wednesday was 2.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.7 to 2.8 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 11:41AM MST until November 17 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1138 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue.
The amount of water released will increase during the next couple
of days, peaking at 3000 cfs.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
